questions.question:
**Directions: Select the correct indirect form of the given sentence.**

The lion asked the lioness, "Where will you hide yourself, until I return?”

options.text: The lion asked the lioness where she would hide herself, until he returned.
The lion asked the lioness where she will hide herself, until he returns.
The lion asked the lioness whether she would hide herself, until he returned.
The lion asked the lioness where would she hide herself, until he returned.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **The lion asked the lioness where she would hide herself, until he returned**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/64e177b3c5c5cb81c12b3d5b5ddabaaf474cdad3d6098992ca6592786c8147d6.png] 

__
 
• The **given sentence** is a **direct speech**.
 
• The **basic rules** for changing or **converting direct speech into indirect speech**__**:**
 
 
• The **commas and inverted commas** are **removed **and the** 'question mark' **is replaced by** 'full stop'**.
 
• The **second-person pronoun 'you'** should be **replaced by** the **third-person pronoun 'she'**.
 
• The **first-person pronoun 'I'** should be **replaced by** the **third-person pronoun 'he'**.
 
• The **present simple tense** format** 'Subject + V₁ (will) + Object' **will be changed into the **past simple tense** format '**Subject + V****₂ ****(would) + Object**'.
 
• The **present simple tense** format** 'Subject + V****₁**** (return) + Object' **will be changed into the **past simple tense** format '**Subject + V****₂ ****(returned) + Object**'.
 
 

Hence, the correct answer is option 1.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/87c1a28e731fadd9279228c1cea2f8e988a3f790bf9ccc89c9b0f02c423b1609.png] 

The following table will enable us to know how tense changes into Indirect speech:-

 
 
 
 
 
 

 **Direct Speech**
 **Indirect Speech**
 
 

 Present simple (Subject +V1st + Object)
 Past simple (Subject +V2 + Object)
 
 

 Present continuous (Subject +is/am/are+V1 +ing+ Object)
 Past Continuous (Subject +was/were+V1 +ing+ Object)
 
 

 Present perfect (Subject + has/have+V3+Object)
 Past perfect (Subject+had+V3+Object)
 
 

 Past simple (Subject+V2+Object)
 Past perfect (Subject+had+V3+Object)
 
 

 Past Continuous (Subject +was/were+V1 +ing+ Object)
 Past perfect continuous (Subject +had been+V1 +ing+ Object)
 
 

 Future simple (Subject+ will/shall+V1+object)
 Present Conditional (Subject+ would+V1+object)
 
 

 Future Continuous (Subject +will/shall+be+V1 +ing+ Object)
 Conditional Continuous (Subject +would+be+V1 +ing+ Object)

questions.question:
**Directions: Select the correct passive form of the given sentence.**

The Inspector had already proved the case before the investigation team took charge of it.

options.text: The investigation team took charge of the case but the Inspector had already proved before it.
The case had already proved by the Inspector before the investigation team took charge of it.
The case was already proved by the Inspector before the investigation team took charge of it.
The case had already been proved by the Inspector before the investigation team took charge of it.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'The case had already been proved by the Inspector before the investigation team took charge of it'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/64e177b3c5c5cb81c12b3d5b5ddabaaf474cdad3d6098992ca6592786c8147d6.png] 

 
• In **Active Voice**, a sentence emphasizes the subject, performing an action.
 
• In **Passive Voice**, a sentence emphasizes the action or the object of the sentence.
 
• The **given sentence** is in the **active voice** and '**The Inspector**' is the **subject **and '**the case**' is the **object.**
 
• When we convert this sentence into **passive voice**, the subject '**The Inspector**' of the active voice **becomes **the **object**, the **object** '**the case**' **becomes** the **subject**.
 
• The passive format "**'had + been + V3 (proved)**" should be used.
 
• This is the active and passive voice **rule** for the **past perfect tense**.

Hence, the correct answer is** option 4***.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/87c1a28e731fadd9279228c1cea2f8e988a3f790bf9ccc89c9b0f02c423b1609.png]

questions.question:
**Directions: Given below are four jumbled sentences. Out of the given options select the one that gives their correct order.**

A. The boat floated down the river and reached the other bank.

B. Thinking that she was dead, her friends secretly took her and abandoned her in a boat.

C. The people on the bank took her to a hospital and saved her.

D. Smelling a flower given by the magician, Shweta fell down unconscious.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'DBAC'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• The sentence 'D' is independent of any other sentences as it is giving general information about the noun "Shweta". Hence, 'D' is the first part.
 
• The pronoun "she" mentioned in the sentence 'B' refers back to the noun 'Shweta' mentioned in the sentence 'D'. Hence, 'B' follows 'D'.
 
• The "boat" mentioned in the sentence 'A' refers back to the "boat" mentioned in the sentence 'B'. Hence, 'A' follows 'B'.
 
• The sentence 'C' is the concluding sentence. Hence, 'C' is the last sentence.

 

Paragraph after rearranging the sentences__: *Smelling a flower given by the magician, Shweta fell down unconscious. Thinking that she was dead, her friends secretly took her and abandoned her in a boat. The boat floated down the river and reached the other bank. The people on the bank took her to a hospital and saved her*.

* [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/0a6c2db12945bba9d674d33112fce66b07f00093d75dae93749f9bdb7bd34e7a.png] **__Hint__***

__
 
• Important Rules to Solve the Para Jumbles__:

 
 
• Read the sentences attentively and try to comprehend the idea or theme of the sentence and eliminate the irrelevant options.
 
• Try to identify the opening (independent sentence) and closing sentences (concluding sentence).
 
• Try to identify the mandatory pairs. Two sentences can be connected through various connectors and other determinants.

questions.question:
**Directions: In the sentence identify the segment which contains the grammatical error.**

One of the reason behind malnutrition is the improper way of food intake.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'One of the reason'**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• In the given sentence, the use of the **singular noun 'reason'** is **incorrect**.
 
• The general rule for the **usage of the phrase** "**One of the**" is **One of the + Plural Noun + that/who etc. + Singular/Plural Verb**.
 
• So, the **noun following** the **phrase** **"one of the"** is always **a plural noun**.
 
• Therefore, the **plural noun 'reasons'** should be used **in place of** the **singular noun 'reason'**.

 

Hence, the correct answer is **option 4**.

**Correct Sentence:** ***One of the reasons** behind malnutrition is the improper way of food intake*.

questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Given Idiom: *Neither fish nor fowl* means **something or someone which is not easily categorized; something or someone that does not rightly belong or fit well in a given group or situation**.

 
 
• *Example*: *Graduate teaching assistants are **neither fish nor fowl**, neither completely students nor teachers*.
 
 
 
• From the given options, the third option is the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

 

Hence, the correct answer is option 3.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e085a7f17645c801966c030eb44d69fae944b96fdb4c4077f5fba1bc2c24bc71.png] **Mistake Points__**

__
 
• We may think from the phrase "Neither fish nor fowl" that it is all about a fish or fowl, but the correct answer is option 3. So be careful while dealing with such questions.

questions.question:
**Directions: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No improvement’.**

__As long to__ funding is not made available, our construction dreams have been deferred.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'So long as'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• In the underlined segment, the phrase 'So much as' is incorrect.
 
• The phrase 'As long to' means **relatively great in the extent to something else**.
 
• The phrase 'As high as' means **to behave in a silly or exciting way**.
 
• The phrase 'In as much as' means since, because, or to the extent that.
 
• The phrase 'So long as' means provided that or **on condition that**.

 

Hence, the correct answer is option 4.

Correct Sentence: ***So long as** funding is not made available, our construction dreams have been deferred*.
